line: Ninety days without power. That's the plan the government is quietly making this year.
Most families won't last ninety hours, because the store shelves are empty by the end of day one.
visual: Empty shelves in a big warehouse store aisle at night, cardboard on the floor, emergency lights only

line: So I loaded one cart for a family of four, item by item, in the order I'd buy it.
visual: {host} pushing a flat warehouse cart loaded with water cases and rice sacks down a tall store aisle

line: Item one is water. Not food. Water.
visual: Close-up of clear water being poured into a glass on a dark kitchen counter, lantern light
title: ITEM 1 · WATER

line: The rule is one gallon per person, per day. Four people, ninety days.
title: THE WATER MATH
rows: 4 PEOPLE x 90 DAYS = 1 GAL/DAY; WATER YOU NEED = 360 GAL !red

line: That's three hundred and sixty gallons, and you are not buying that much bottled water.
rows: 360 GAL = FOR A FAMILY OF FOUR !yellow

line: So the cart does water in three layers. Layer one is ten big cases of bottled water.
Layer two is a few of the blue seven gallon jugs with the spigot on the side.
visual: Two blue 7-gallon water jugs with spigots on a kitchen counter, warm lantern light

line: And layer three is the one that carries you to day ninety, a gravity water filter.
product: Stainless steel gravity water filter | Unscented household bleach
title: LAYER 3

line: Now add up the water you already own, before you buy a single drop.
visual: {host} kneeling next to a home water heater tank in a garage, opening the drain valve into a bucket

line: The cases give you about a hundred gallons, the jugs thirty five, and your water heater holds fifty.
title: CLEAN WATER ON HAND
rows: CASES = 100 GAL; JUGS = 35 GAL; WATER HEATER = 50 GAL

line: And never store it in the attic. The garage floor, out of the sun, is where it belongs.
title: NEVER STORE IT HERE
rows: ~THE ATTIC; ~IN THE SUN; THE GARAGE FLOOR; A DARK CLOSET

line: That's water handled for ninety days, for about the price of a nice dinner out.

line: Next, the three cheap foods that cover more than half of all ninety days.
